{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
penguins = pd.read_csv('data/penguins.csv')

# The contract specifies 'all penguins in the dataset' as the population
# However, we cannot compute a mean flipper length if there are missing values
# So we must exclude rows with missing flipper_length_mm
# But we must assess whether this exclusion affects the validity

# Check the number of missing values in flipper_length_mm
missing_flipper = penguins['flipper_length_mm'].isnull().sum()
print(f'Number of missing flipper_length_mm values: {missing_flipper}')

# Check which species have missing values
missing_data = penguins[penguins['flipper_length_mm'].isnull()]
print('\nSpecies with missing flipper_length_mm:')
print(missing_data['species'].value_counts())

# Since only 2 out of 344 rows are missing, and they are from two different species (Adelie and Gentoo),
# the exclusion of these rows will not systematically bias the mean for any species
# The missingness is not concentrated in one species, so the mean per species remains valid

# Compute mean flipper length per species using only available data
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=['flipper_length_mm'])
mean_flipper_by_species = penguins_clean.groupby('species')['flipper_length_mm'].mean()

# Identify the species with the highest mean
highest_mean_species = mean_flipper_by_species.idxmax()
highest_mean_value = mean_flipper_by_species.max()

print('\nMean flipper length by species:')
print(mean_flipper_by_species)
print(f'\nSpecies with highest mean flipper length: {highest_mean_species}')
print(f'Highest mean flipper length: {highest_mean_value:.2f} mm')"}
